mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, exalted is He, {هدى وبشرى}: two aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions) from الْكتاب.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {بشهاب قبس}: whoever reads it with annexation (iḍāfa) has annexed the species to its genus, like your saying ثوب خَز ("a garment of silk"). Al-Farrāʾ said it is the annexation of a thing to itself, like صَلَاة الأولى; but it is not like it, because صَلَاة الأولى is originally a described noun and its adjective, and the described noun was annexed to its adjective, its original form being الصَّلَاة الأولى. Whoever gives tanwīn to شهابا makes قبسا a badal (substitute) for it; it is also said to be its adjective. If you put قبسا in the accusative outside the Qur'an, it would be permissible as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz). الشهاب is anything that has light, and القبس is what is taken (as a flame) from embers and the like. So its meaning for whoever does not give tanwīn is "a flame of a firebrand" (بشهاب من قبس). القَبْس is the maṣdar and القَبَس is the noun, just as the meaning of ثوب خَز is "a garment of silk" (ثوب من خَز).
His saying {تصطلون}: the original of the ṭāʾ is a tāʾ; its pattern is تفتعلون. They replaced the tāʾ with a ṭāʾ because of its kinship with the ṣād in velarisation (iṭbāq). The final radical (lām al-fiʿl) was made weak and was then elided because it was vowelless and the wāw after it was vowelless.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {نُودي أَن بورك}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, i.e. "he was called because (لِأَن) blessed is…" or "with (بِأَن) blessed is…", and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is latent and stands in place of the agent, i.e. "the call was made because blessed is…". It is also said that أَن is in the position of the nominative as the object whose agent is not named (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) of نودي. Al-Kisāʾī reported "باركك الله" and "بَارك فِيك" (both: "may Allah bless you").

mekki-muskil:10-10.t:
His saying {تهتز}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in {رَآهَا}. Likewise {كَأَنَّهَا جَان} is also in the position of a ḥāl. Its implied form is "when he saw it quivering, resembling a snake, he turned back fleeing". رأى here is from seeing with the eye.
His saying {مُدبرا}: a ḥāl from Moses, peace be upon him.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {إِلَّا من ظلم}: من is in the position of the accusative because it is an exception not of the same kind as the first. Al-Farrāʾ said it is an exception of the same kind, but the thing excepted from is omitted; this is far-fetched. Some grammarians allowed إِلَّا to have the meaning of the wāw, and this is even more far-fetched because of the confusion of meanings.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {تخرج بَيْضَاء}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تخرج, which is the pronoun of the hand.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {آيَاتنَا مبصرة}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الآيات, meaning "made clear". Whoever reads مبصرة with fatḥa on the ṣād makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying {غير بعيد}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted adverb of time, its implied form being "so he stayed a time not long", or of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a stay not long".
His saying {من سبإ}: whoever inflects it fully makes it the name of a father (ancestor) or of a tribe-group; whoever does not inflect it fully makes it the name of the tribe, or of the city, or of a woman, so it is not fully inflected because of definiteness and femininity. Whoever reads the hamza vowelless does so with the intention of a pause. It is also said that he made it vowelless to lighten it because of a succession of seven vowels. All of this is far-fetched.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {أَلا يسجدوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by يهتدون, and لا is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for الْأَعْمَال, and لا is not redundant. It is also said that it is in the position of the genitive as a badal for السَّبِيل, and لا is redundant. As for the reading of al-Kisāʾī, أَلا يَا اسجدوا with أَلا lightened, it has the meaning "Lo, O these people, prostrate", so أَلا is for alerting, يَا is for the vocative, and the one addressed is omitted because the vocative particle indicates it. On this reading اسجدوا is indeclinable (mabnī, an imperative), whereas on the first reading it is accusative by أن.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {إِنَّه من سُلَيْمَان} and وَإنَّهُ: the kasra in both is because they begin a new sentence. Al-Farrāʾ allowed fatḥa in both in ordinary speech, their position being nominative as a badal (substitute) for كتاب, and he allowed them to be in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {أَلا تعلوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, i.e. "that you not exalt yourselves" (بِأَن لَا تعلوا). It is also said to be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for كتاب, its implied form being "there has been delivered to me: do not exalt yourselves". Sībawayh said it has the meaning of أي, explicative, with no grammatical position, like {أَن امشوا}.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t:
His saying {أَذِلَّة وهم صاغرون}: two aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions) from the accusative pronoun in لنخرجنهم.
The tāʾ in {عفريت} is extra, as it is extra in طاغوت. Its plural is عفاريت and عفار, just as you say for the plural of طاغوت: طواغيت and طواغ. طواغ and عفار are like جوَار: the yāʾ is elided — it is said because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, namely the yāʾ and the tanwīn, and it is said for lightening, which is more correct. If you compensate (for the elided letter), you say عفاري and طواغي. This type took tanwīn although it is a diptote only because, when the yāʾ was elided for lightening, the structure because of which it was a diptote was reduced; once it was reduced, the tanwīn entered. It is also said that rather the tanwīn entered as compensation for the elision of the yāʾ. When these nouns, which are diptote plurals, come to the accusative state, the yāʾ returns and they refuse full inflection.
[Translator's note: the Qur'an reads لَنُخْرِجَنَّهُم; the source text has انخرجنهم, apparently a copying error.]

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {وصدها مَا كَانَت تعبد}: مَا is in the position of the nominative because it is the agent of the hindering. It may also be in the position of the accusative by صدها by omission of the preposition, and in صدها there is the pronoun of the agent, which is Allah, exalted be His mention, or Solomon, peace be upon him, i.e. "Allah hindered her from her worship (of it)" or "Solomon hindered her from her worship (of it)".
His saying {إِنَّهَا كَانَت}: whoever reads إن with kasra does so because it begins a new sentence. Whoever reads it with fatḥa makes it a badal (substitute) for مَا when that is the agent. It is also said that rather it is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "because she was" (لِأَنَّهَا كَانَت).

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {مَعَ سُلَيْمَان}: it is said that مَعَ is a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, because it can be a noun used as an adverb, so it was strengthened by full declinability (tamkīn) in some of its states, and so it was made indeclinable; it is a particle indeclinable on fatḥa because it is a noun in some of its states, while its due is sukūn. It is also said that it is an adverbial noun, and therefore it has fatḥa like the adverbs. If you make the ʿayn vowelless, then it is a particle and nothing else.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t:
His saying {أَن اعبدوا الله}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "that you worship Allah" (بِأَن اعبدوا الله).
His saying: they said {اطيرنا}: its origin is تطيرنا; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ and so became vowelless, because the first of the assimilated letters can only be vowelless, and a letter is not assimilated into another letter until the first is vowelless. When the first became vowelless, a connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was brought in at the start so that one could begin with it, and it was given kasra because it is vowelless and what follows it is vowelless. It is also said that rather it is given kasra for the kasra or fatḥa of the third letter of the verb; it was not given fatḥa for the fatḥa of the third letter so that it would not resemble the alif of the first person, and it is given ḍamma for the ḍamma of the third letter so as not to pass from kasra to ḍamma. The pattern of اطيرنا according to its origin is تفعلنا, and it cannot be weighed according to its pronunciation, since among the patterns there is no افعلنا with two successive doubled letters.
We have already mentioned {مهلك} in al-Kahf.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying {قَالُوا تقاسموا بِاللَّه لنبيتنه} {وَأَهله ثمَّ لنقولن}: whoever reads it with the tāʾ in both words makes تقاسموا an imperative, and it is an indeclinable verb; likewise whoever reads it with the nūn in both. Whoever reads both with the yāʾ makes تقاسموا a past verb, because it is a report about someone absent, while the first is a report addressed to someone present or about the speaker himself.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t:
His saying فَانْظُر كَيفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَة مَكْرهمْ إِنَّا دمرناهم: whoever reads إنا with kasra does so as the start of a new sentence; كيف is the khabar (predicate) of كان placed first, because the interrogative has the head of the sentence (ṣadr al-kalām), and عاقبة is the ism (noun) of كان. انظر does not govern كيف, but it governs the position of the whole clause. It is also said that كان means "occurred, came about", عاقبة is its noun and it has no khabar, and كيف is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied form is "so look, O Muhammad, in what state the outcome of their affair occurred". Then He explained how the outcome occurred, saying by way of explanation and as a new sentence: إِنَّا دمرناهم وقومهم. As for whoever reads أنا with fatḥa, he makes كيف the khabar of كان, العاقبة its noun, and أن a badal (substitute) for العاقبة, with كيف in the position of a ḥāl. If you wish, you may make أنا the khabar of كان, العاقبة its noun, and كيف in the position of a ḥāl; the implied form is "so look, O Muhammad, in what state the outcome of their affair was: their destruction". It is also said that أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "so look how the outcome of their plotting was, because We destroyed them". In ordinary speech it is permissible to put عاقبة in the accusative as the khabar of كان and make أنا the noun of كان. It is also said that the position of أنا is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is that We destroyed them" (هُوَ أَنا دمرناهم), and the clause is the khabar of كان.
His saying {إِلَّا الله وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ}: the nominative in the name of Allah, exalted be His mention, is as a badal (substitute) for من.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {فَتلك بُيُوتهم خاوية}: خاوية is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The nominative is permissible in خاوية in ordinary speech in five ways. First, بيوتهم is a badal (substitute) for تلك and خاوية is the khabar (predicate) of البيوت. Second, خاوية is a second khabar. Third, خاوية is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are empty" (هِيَ خاوية). Fourth, you make خاوية a badal for البيوت. Fifth, you make بيوتهم a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) for تلك, and خاوية the khabar of تلك.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {ولوطا}: لوطا is accusative in the sense of "and remember", or in the sense of "and We sent Lot".

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying الله خير أما يشركُونَ: comparison (al-mufāḍala) is allowed here, though there is no good in their gods, only because they were addressed according to what they believed, since they held (good) opinions about their gods; so they were addressed according to their claim and opinion. It has also been said that خير here is not of the pattern أفعل (the elative); it is only فَعْل, so no comparison between two things is implied, as Ḥassān said:
... فشركما لخير كَمَا الْفِدَاء ...
(So the worse of you two is a ransom for the better of you two.)
i.e. the one of you two in whom there is evil is a ransom for the one in whom there is good.

mekki-muskil:66-66.t:
His saying {بل ادارك علمهمْ}: whoever reads it on the pattern أفعل (أدْرَكَ) builds it on the idea that their knowledge about the coming of the Hour has reached its limit, with nothing more for them in it, i.e. they will never know it, since there is nothing more in their knowledge; one says ادَّرك الثمر when the fruit has reached its full ripeness. It is also said that its meaning is denial, i.e. "has their knowledge attained anything about the Hereafter?", i.e. it has attained nothing, and they have come to no reality of it. It is also said that its meaning is "rather, their knowledge about the matter of the Hereafter is complete, with nothing more in it". What shows that it is by way of denial is His saying {بل هم فِي شكّ مِنْهَا}, i.e. they have not grasped the time of its coming about, so they are blind to it, and blindness to a thing is greater than doubt about it. Whoever reads it with a connecting alif and doubled (ادّارك), its origin is تدارك; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl and the connecting alif entered at the start because the first of the doubled letters is vowelless, like His saying اطيرنا. Its meaning is "rather, their knowledge about the coming of the Hour is complete, so they have nothing more". It is also said its meaning is "rather, their knowledge about the matter of the Hereafter followed on successively and they did not reach anything".
His saying {فِي الْآخِرَة}: في means the bāʾ, i.e. "about the Hereafter" (بالآخرة), i.e. about the knowledge of the Hereafter.

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {ردف لكم}: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and its meaning is ردفكم ("is close behind you"). Similar to it is {وَإِذ بوأنا لإِبْرَاهِيم مَكَان الْبَيْت}, and similar is {إِن كُنْتُم للرؤيا تعبرون}. This is frequent; the lām in it is redundant and is not attached to anything. There is disagreement about it.

mekki-muskil:82-82.t: His saying {تكلمهم أَن النَّاس}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "it will speak to them that (بأن) the people…". You may also not assume an omitted preposition and make أن its direct object, by making تكلمهم mean "it will inform them". Whoever reads إن with kasra does so as a new sentence (istiʾnāf).

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {وَيَوْم ينْفخ فِي الصُّور}: the governor of يوم is an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember the day when the Horn is blown".

mekki-muskil:88-88.t: His saying {صنع الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because when He, exalted is He, said وَهِي تمر مر السَّحَاب, this indicated that He, exalted is He, made that, so it (the implied verb) governed صنع الله. It may also be accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ), and the nominative is permissible in the sense "that is the making of Allah".

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His saying {من جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَة فَلهُ خير مِنْهَا}: من is conditional, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and فله is the apodosis (jawāb), which is the khabar (predicate).
